card.title: AM vs FM — riding information on carrier waves

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Every link runs transmitter → channel → receiver: the message (baseband audio/data) modulates a high-frequency carrier because low frequencies need kilometre antennas and drown in noise. AM stamps the message on carrier AMPLITUDE (simple, noisy); FM stamps it on FREQUENCY (noise-resistant, needs more bandwidth). Bandwidth prices the channel; ground/sky/space-wave propagation picks the frequency band.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: AM: carrier amplitude ∝ message · FM: carrier frequency ∝ message  ·  antenna ~ λ/4 (high f → short antenna)  ·  bandwidth: AM ~ 2×message (kHz), FM ~ 200 kHz broadcast  ·  propagation: ground (<MHz) · sky (3–30 MHz, ionosphere) · space/LOS (>40 MHz, satellites)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Modulation needs carrier frequency ≫ message frequency (else sidebands tangle). Sky-wave hops need ionospheric reflection (night/day layers differ). Line-of-sight links need antenna height clearing the horizon (d ≈ √(2Rh)). Digital modes add sampling (Nyquist) beyond this syllabus.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: FM radio sounds cleaner than AM because amplitude noise (lightning, motors) barely touches frequency-coded audio. Mobile towers are space-wave cells; shortwave crosses continents via ionosphere hops. Optical fibre replaces EM channels with guided light (TIR) for backbone bandwidth.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Why not broadcast audio directly? A 5 kHz signal needs λ/4 ≈ 15 km antennas and all stations overlap. Modulate onto a 1 MHz carrier: antenna shrinks to ~75 m, stations separate by carrier frequency, receivers tune by resonance — three problems, one modulation.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: AM wastes power in the carrier + twin sidebands (SSB trims it). FM buys quality with spectrum (wide channels). All analog links degrade gracefully but never perfectly — noise is managed, not removed (digital error-correction is the next course).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: AM math: [A_c + m(t)]·cos(ω_c t) expands to carrier plus two sidebands at ω_c ± ω_m — the 2×message bandwidth derived, not memorised. FM's constant amplitude follows from encoding in the argument's derivative; its noise immunity follows because most channel noise is additive in amplitude.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: AM = amplitude varies, noisy, narrow; FM = frequency varies, clean, wide. Propagation by band: low→ground, mid→sky/ionosphere, high→space/LOS. Block diagram: source→transducer→modulator→channel→demodulator→output — draw it for full process marks.

rows.text: NEB-style: block diagram of a communication system; AM vs FM comparison (quality, bandwidth, noise); why modulation is necessary (antenna + interference + multiplexing); propagation modes with frequency ranges.
